transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm explaining this okay, but I guess the main reason I made the appointment is that I tend to get... pulled off track kind of easily? 

It's probably normal, and I really don't want to make a huge deal out of it, but like, if I'm trying to finish a dashboard for a project, just one little Slack ping, or even a song lyric playing in the background, or a random idea for another project popping into my head... and suddenly I've completely lost the thread of what I was supposed to be doing. I really do try hard to stay focused, I promise, it just sort of slips away from me sometimes. 

Is that... does that make sense? I hope that's the right kind of thing to bring up.
Does this happen to you in other areas of your life, like at home or in social situations, or is it mainly at work?

Um, yeah, I guess it does happen in other areas, too. I hope it's okay to talk about school and side projects, since I'm mostly just a student right now? 

But, um... I do some small freelance things on the side, and... well, I actually ended up losing a couple of minor contracts recently. And I missed out on a portfolio competition, too. It wasn't a huge disaster or anything, I just... I didn't follow through as cleanly as I should have, I guess. 

And socially... I really hate admitting this, because I don't want to sound like a bad friend, I promise I really try my best to be there for people. But I think some of my friends and the people I collaborate with are a little... hesitant to work with me right now? They always say they really like my ideas, which is so sweet of them, but I think they just worry they can't totally rely on me to finish my part of things. Which is completely fair of them, honestly. 

Um, is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I hope I'm not complaining too much.
Do you feel like your difficulties with staying focused are causing you a lot of stress or problems in your daily life?

Um, well... I wouldn't say it's causing a *huge* amount of stress, like, I'm surviving and everything! I really don't want to sound ungrateful or dramatic. But... I guess it is causing some problems, yeah. 

Like I mentioned before with the freelance stuff... I really did try my hardest, but I ended up losing those small contracts, and I missed the deadline for that portfolio competition. I just... I couldn't seem to follow through as cleanly as I needed to, and I know that's completely my fault. 

And then with my friends... it's just a little stressful because I know they're hesitant to collaborate with me now. They're so nice about it, they always say they love my ideas, but I know they just can't totally rely on me to get my part done. Which I completely understand, I'd probably feel the same way if I were them! I just feel bad that I'm letting them down when I promise I'm really trying not to. 

Does that answer your question? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it actually is.
Have you always had trouble staying focused, or is this something that has developed more recently?

Um, well... I think it's kind of always been there? I really don't want it to sound like I was a bad kid or anything, because I promise I always tried to be good! But... yeah, even back in elementary school, my teachers would write little notes on my report cards. 

They were usually really nice about it, but they'd mention things like me rushing through my worksheets a bit too fast, or, um, maybe losing track of the directions? And I guess I got a little too excited during group work sometimes and would accidentally talk over my classmates. I didn't mean to be rude, I just had so many thoughts I wanted to share! 

And, um, my parents actually used to sit right next to me while I did my homework. I think if they didn't, I would just kind of... wander off, or start playing with something else before I finished my math problems. They were really patient with me, though. 

Is it okay that I brought up stuff from when I was little? I hope that's the kind of background you were looking for!
Do you often feel restless or fidgety, like you can't sit still?

Um, well... I guess I do move around a bit? I really try my best to be polite and sit quietly, especially when it's important! But... yeah, I suppose I can be a little fidgety sometimes. 

Like, if I'm in a meeting or a portfolio review for school, I don't even realize I'm doing it at first, but I might be bouncing my leg a little, or maybe clicking my pen? And I have these rings that I tend to twist around, or I'll just kind of shift in my chair a lot. I usually only notice when someone glances over at me, and then I feel so bad because I really don't want to be distracting or disrespectful to whoever is talking! I just... I guess my body just likes to keep moving a little bit? 

I hope that doesn't make me sound too unprofessional. Is that normal, or is that what you meant by restless?
Have you had any close relationships end or become strained due to your difficulties with following through on commitments or staying focused?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I try really hard to be a good friend and a good girlfriend! I definitely wouldn't say any close relationships have actually ended because of it. 

I guess, like I mentioned before, my friends get a little frustrated when we try to do projects together, but we're still really close! We just... maybe don't collaborate on art stuff as much anymore, which is totally fair on their part. And my boyfriend is super sweet and patient with me. Sometimes I might forget to text him back right away if I get distracted, or I might be a little late when we meet up, but he's really understanding about it. I always apologize a million times, and I promise I'm trying to be better about time management!

So, yeah, nothing has ended or gotten super strained, thankfully. I really do care about the people in my life, and I wouldn't want them to think otherwise. Did I explain that okay?
Would you say that your difficulties with staying focused and following through on commitments are currently affecting your overall academic or work performance?

Um, well... I guess maybe a little bit? I really try my best, I promise, and I don't want it to sound like I'm completely dropping the ball on everything! But, um, I suppose there have been a few little hiccups with my art stuff. 

Like, I've done a few small freelance commissions, and... well, I guess a couple of them kind of fell through because I had a hard time getting the final edits done exactly when they wanted them. I didn't mean to mess it up, I just got a little overwhelmed trying to follow through on all the tiny details perfectly. And I actually missed the deadline for this really cool portfolio competition last semester. I had all the pieces started, but I just couldn't seem to pull them all together and submit them on time. 

And, um, like I said about my friends... they're still my friends! But I think some of the people I collaborate with are a little hesitant to start new projects with me now. They always tell me they love my concepts and ideas, which is so nice of them! But I think they worry I might not follow through as cleanly as they need me to. 

I feel awful about it, honestly, because I really do want to be reliable and do good work. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making myself sound like a terrible student!
Do you often interrupt others when they're talking or finish their sentences for them?

Oh, um... I really try my best not to! I know it's rude to interrupt, and I always want to make sure everyone feels heard. But... I guess, maybe sometimes I do a little bit? Just when I get really, really excited. 

Like, if my classmates and I are brainstorming, sometimes I'll kind of... blurt out an idea I have right in the middle of their thought? Or, um, I might start adding things to their Figma board before they've even finished explaining what they wanted to do. I really don't mean to talk over anyone, I promise! I just get so enthusiastic about the concepts that my brain kind of jumps ahead, and it just slips out. 

But then almost immediately afterward, I can tell from their reactions that I probably came off as kind of pushy, even though I was just trying to be helpful and engaged. I always feel so awful and try to apologize the second I realize I did it. I really hate making people feel like I don't care about what they're saying. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible group member... is that the kind of thing you mean?

Would you say that your difficulties with staying focused and following through on commitments are currently causing significant problems in your daily life or interfering with your ability to achieve your goals?

Um... "significant" sounds like such a strong word, and I really don't want to make it seem like my whole life is a mess or anything! I really am trying my absolute best to keep everything together. But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, and kind of tying back to what I was just saying a minute ago... it is getting in the way of my goals a little bit. 

Like with those small freelance contracts I lost, and missing out on that portfolio competition... those were really important steps for my career, and it just breaks my heart that I missed out on them because people couldn't rely on me to follow through cleanly. And, um, knowing that my friends and collaborators are hesitant to work with me now, even though they still say they like my ideas... it just makes me feel so guilty. I hate the thought that I'm letting people down when they give me a chance. 

So, um, I suppose it is causing some problems, even though I'm trying so, so hard not to let it. I just really want to be successful and for people to know they can trust me. Does that answer your question okay? I hope I'm not sounding too negative!
Do you find that you have trouble staying focused and following through on tasks in quiet or low-stimulation environments, or does it mainly happen in busy or distracting settings?

Um, well, I guess it kind of happens in both? But I really do try to set myself up for success! Like, I'll go to a quiet corner of the library, put my phone away, and really try to focus. But... even when it's super quiet and there aren't any obvious distractions, I still struggle a little bit. 

Like, I can sit down to read a research article for class, or, um, watch a UX tutorial that I'm actually really interested in... but then after a few minutes, I'll realize my eyes have just been moving across the page or the screen, and I have absolutely no idea what I just took in. It's like my brain just sort of... floated away, even though I was trying so hard to pay attention! 

I feel so silly when it happens, because I really do want to learn the material, and I don't want you to think I'm just not trying. I promise I am! It's just... sometimes it feels like my brain won't cooperate, even when I give it the perfect environment. Is that normal? I hope that makes sense!
Do you often make careless mistakes or overlook details in your work or other activities?

Oh, um... well, I really do try to be as careful as I can! I always want my work to look professional and put-together. But... I guess sometimes, maybe, a little mistake might slip through? 

Like, I'll be working on a design project for class, and I'll submit a mockup or a data chart, and I'll honestly think it's completely polished and ready to go. I really do check it over! But then... maybe a day later, I'll look back at it and realize I mislabeled an axis, or I used the wrong color key for the branding, or... or I missed some tiny little instruction that was buried in the client brief. 

It's never because I don't care, I promise! I always feel so embarrassed when someone points it out, or when I catch it myself after the fact. I really don't want people to think I'm sloppy or that I'm not taking the assignment seriously, because I really am. It's just... sometimes those little details just sort of blur together when I'm trying to look at the big picture. 

Does that sound like the kind of careless mistake you're asking about? I hope I don't sound like I'm just rushing through my work!

Do you think your difficulties with staying focused and following through on tasks are related to being bored or uninterested in the activities, or is it more that you just can't seem to sustain your attention regardless of how interesting they are?

Um, well, I guess it's a little bit of both? But I really want to emphasize that it's not because I don't care! I promise I'm not just slacking off or ignoring things because they're boring. I really do try to be diligent. 

But... I suppose, even when I'm working on something I really love, like a design project, I can still get a little sidetracked. Like, if a professor or a peer gives me a list of revisions to make... I always start out so strong! I'll knock out the first couple of changes right away, and I'll feel really good about it. But then... I don't know, my brain will just sort of catch on a different idea? Like I'll drift into redesigning a completely different part of the layout that wasn't even on the list, just because it suddenly seemed like a really cool idea to explore. 

And then... sometimes I'll realize later that I left one small, but, um, kind of important change from the original list unfinished. I always feel so terrible when that happens! I really don't want people to think I'm ignoring their feedback, because I value it so much. It's just that my attention kind of wanders off on its own little adventure, even when I'm genuinely interested in what I'm doing. 

Does that make sense? I hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm just blowing off my responsibilities! I really do try my best to get everything done.
Do you think your mind wanders off because you're easily distracted by your surroundings or because you get caught up in your own thoughts and ideas?

Um, well, I guess it's... it's really both? I mean, I really try to stay focused, but... actually, this is kind of the main reason I decided to come in and talk to you. I just get pulled off track so easily, and I really don't want it to seem like I'm not dedicated to my work! 

It's just that, um, sometimes it's my surroundings, like if I hear a Slack ping from a classmate, or even just a song lyric playing in the background... my brain just sort of latches onto it? And other times, it's definitely my own thoughts. Like, I'll get a random, really exciting idea for a completely different project, and before I know it, I've just... completely lost the thread of the dashboard I was supposed to be finishing. 

I always feel so bad when it happens, because I really do want to finish what I started! I try so hard to block everything out, but it just feels like my brain is too eager to jump to the next thing. Does that sound like what you were asking? I hope I'm explaining it okay... I just really want to figure out how to be better at this!
Do you think you would have an easier time staying focused if you were doing something you found extremely interesting or enjoyable?

Um, well, I guess... it does help a little bit if it's something I really, really enjoy? But... to be completely honest, even then, I still struggle sometimes. I really hope that doesn't make me sound lazy, because I genuinely want to learn and do well! 

Like, for example, I can sit down to read a research article for a paper, or even watch a UX tutorial that I'm actually really excited about. I'll have the best intentions, I promise! But... after a few minutes, I'll suddenly realize that my eyes have just been sort of moving across the page, or I've been staring at the screen, and... I have absolutely no idea what I just took in. 

It's so frustrating, and I always feel a little embarrassed when I have to rewind a video three times just to understand a simple concept. I really try to force myself to pay attention, but it's like my brain just takes a little vacation without my permission. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is... I really do try my best to stay engaged! Is it normal to struggle with that even when you're interested in the topic?
Do you think you would be able to focus and complete tasks if you were in a quiet, distraction-free environment with a task that you find extremely interesting?

Um, I really wish I could say yes to that! I always try to set up my space to be super quiet, thinking it'll be the perfect environment to just buckle down. But... well, actually, the quiet almost makes it a little harder sometimes? I really hope that doesn't sound weird or like I'm just making excuses! 

It's just that, even when I'm trying to do something really relaxing that I completely enjoy, like reading a fun book or doing a really calm sketching exercise... I find that I can't just, you know, be quiet with it. I'll catch myself talking out loud to myself, or I'll feel like I absolutely have to put on some music, or I'll start checking things on my phone. Or, um, I'll take a simple little doodle and suddenly turn it into this massive, complicated design project instead of just letting it be a relaxing activity. 

I really do try my best to just enjoy the quiet and focus! It's just... it's like my brain feels the need to fill the silence, if that makes sense? I hope I'm answering your question right... I just don't want you to think I'm purposely trying to make things chaotic when I'm supposed to be working or resting! Is it okay that I struggle with the quiet like that?
Do you feel overwhelmed or anxious when you're unable to focus or complete a task?

Um, I mean... I wouldn't say I get super overwhelmed or anything! I really try to just take it in stride, you know? I don't want to sound like I'm constantly stressed out or panicking over every little thing. 

I guess I do get a tiny bit frustrated with myself sometimes, just because I want to be doing a good job and being productive. But it's not like a huge, anxious meltdown or anything like that. I usually just try to take a deep breath and remind myself to try harder next time. 

Does that sound normal? I really hope I'm not coming across as too dramatic or anything... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answer. Is it okay that I don't feel super anxious about it?
Would you say that your difficulties with staying focused and following through on commitments are currently causing significant distress or problems in your daily life?

Um, well... I guess maybe a little bit? I really, really hate to admit it, because I don't want to sound like I'm totally dropping the ball on everything. I really do try my hardest to keep up! 

But... um, if I'm being completely honest, it has caused a few little hiccups. Like, there were these small freelance contracts I was trying to do, and... well, I sort of lost them. And I ended up missing out on this portfolio competition, too. It wasn't because I didn't want to do them! I really did. It's just... I think people felt like they couldn't completely rely on me to follow through cleanly on all the details. 

And, um, I think it's made a few of my friends and people I collaborate with a little hesitant to work with me lately. Which makes me feel terrible, because they always tell me they really like my ideas! It's just the execution part that gets a bit messy. 

I really hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible person to work with. I promise I'm trying to get better at it! Does that make sense? I just... I want to make sure I'm giving you the full picture, even if it's a little embarrassing to admit. Is it normal for it to affect things like that?
Would you say that your difficulties with staying focused and following through on commitments are currently causing you significant problems in your daily life?

Um, I think we just talked about this a little bit, but... yeah, I guess it is causing some problems. I really wish it wasn't, though! I don't want to sound like my whole life is falling apart or anything, because it's really not. I'm generally doing okay!

But, like I mentioned before, I did end up losing those small freelance contracts. And missing that portfolio competition. It's just so embarrassing to admit that people felt like they couldn't rely on me to finish things cleanly. I really did want to do a good job for them! I hope you don't think I'm just lazy or don't care about my work.

And it's just hard because some of my friends and people I usually collaborate with have been... well, a little hesitant to start new projects with me lately. They always say they love my ideas, which is really sweet of them! But I know the follow-through is where I let them down. 

I'm really trying to be better about it, I promise! I just... I hope I'm not coming across as completely irresponsible. Is it okay that I'm struggling with this right now? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you often have difficulty waiting for your turn in lines or when waiting for others to finish speaking?

Um... I mean, I try really hard to be polite! I don't want to be that person who's rude or impatient, you know? I always try to wait my turn. 

But... I guess sometimes, like if I'm waiting in a really long line for a hackathon check-in, or if I'm stuck in an office-hour queue for a professor, I do get a tiny bit... antsy? Like, I'll catch myself checking my phone a lot, or shifting my weight back and forth. And sometimes, if someone is talking and I have an idea, I have to try really, really hard not to just jump in before they're completely finished. 

I don't do it on purpose to be disrespectful! I just get so excited or, I don't know, eager to get to the next thing. I usually catch myself, though! Does that sound like what you mean? I hope it doesn't make me sound like a bad listener or anything... I really do care about what other people are saying! Is it normal to feel a little restless like that?
Have you ever been diagnosed with Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder or taken any medication for attention problems?

Um, no, I haven't. I've never been diagnosed with anything like that, or taken any medication for it. I mean, I've always just tried to manage things on my own, you know? I really do try my best to stay organized and keep up with everything. 

I wouldn't want to take up a doctor's time if it was just me needing to work a little harder or use a better planner. I hope that's okay? Like, I'm not doing something wrong by not having gotten it checked out before, am I? I just... I always thought maybe I just needed to try a little harder to focus.
